newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian government adopts draft ownership law.
newsitem.headline: Serbian government adopts draft ownership law.

text.p: The Serbian government adopted a draft law on ownership transformation on Wednesday and submitted it to the republican parliament for approval at its June 30 session, state news agency Tanjug reported.
The draft privatisation law was first offered to public debate late in March and has since undergone heavy changes. Its final version was presented last week, clearing the way for its adoption.
Under the law the government aims to have 80 percent of companies transformed within two years even though privatisation is not compulsory for companies.

"It is a key legislative project within the reform process and will round off the market-oriented economic system the Serbian government has been building for three and a half years," a government statement was quoted as saying.
The law is due to take effect in October. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom +38111 222 4305
